f-barile: Works on group recommender systems and how to explain their outputs, drawing on social choice theory to aggregate preferences fairly. Recent papers evaluate whether explanations actually help users understand group recommendations, with applications in cultural heritage and media.
p-bonizzi: Develops signal-processing methods for physiological time series, most visibly singular spectrum decomposition and measures of neural synchrony. Much of the work targets cardiac electrophysiology, including atrial fibrillation and electrocardiographic imaging, with further studies in traumatic brain injury.
p-bosilj: Works on computer vision for field robotics, with a strong line in precision agriculture: segmenting crops from weeds, transfer learning across crop types, and morphology-based image features. Earlier work covers hierarchical image representations and remote-sensing image retrieval.
m-bousse: Develops tensor decomposition methods for large-scale signal processing, including blind source separation and system identification using segmentation. These methods are applied to biomedical signals such as heartbeat classification, alongside work in mathematics education.
caw-brewster: Works on ontologies and knowledge representation, from data-driven ontology evaluation to semantic technologies for agri-food. Applied work spans IoT in agriculture, blockchain for food supply chains, and collaborative resource planning for disaster management.
r-cavill: Develops computational methods for integrating omics data, especially transcriptomics with metabolomics, including the IMPaLA pathway-analysis tool. Applications range from cancer metabolic profiling to platelet function and drug toxicity.
r-celebi: Builds knowledge graphs and graph-based machine learning for biomedicine, particularly predicting drug–drug interactions and synergistic cancer drug combinations. Also contributes to FAIR research workflows and AI-supported curation of health data.
sa-chaplick: A graph theorist working on the structure and recognition of geometric intersection graphs, contact representations of planar graphs, and graph drawing. The work sits squarely in algorithms and combinatorics, with links to computational geometry and visualisation.
pj-collins: Works on rigorous computation and verification for hybrid and nonlinear dynamical systems, including reachability analysis and the Ariadne verification framework. Also contributed to Myokit, a tool for cardiac cell modelling, and to computability theory.
o-dhuys: Studies nonlinear dynamics in delay-coupled systems: synchronisation in network motifs, chaos in coupled semiconductor lasers, and pattern formation. The work is mathematical physics in character, centred on time-delayed dynamical systems.
d-dibenedetto: Works on quantum computing, including quantum algorithms for particle-track reconstruction at LHCb and Monte Carlo tree search for quantum circuit design. Earlier research used molecular dynamics to study protein conformations and modelled learning in neural oscillator networks.
p-dreesen: Works at the intersection of systems theory and numerical linear algebra: decoupling multivariate polynomials with tensor methods, polynomial system solving via Macaulay matrices, and nonlinear system identification.
k-driessens: A machine learning researcher best known for relational reinforcement learning. Current work spans planning, transfer and few-shot learning, game AI, and deep models such as visual saliency prediction.
mj-dumontier: Works on semantic web technologies and biomedical ontologies, and co-authored the FAIR Guiding Principles for scientific data. The record spans knowledge graphs for drug discovery, the Ontology for Biomedical Investigations, and infrastructure for FAIR, machine-actionable research data.
aj-garnock-jones: Works on programming languages and distributed systems, in particular the Syndicate model of coordinated concurrent programming, parsing-expression grammars, and language-level support for networking. Also co-authored a widely cited study of single-board computer clusters.
g-goyal: Works on human pose estimation and action recognition, especially with event cameras for high-frequency, low-latency sensing. Contributions include the MoveEnet model and the MoCA dataset of fine-grained cooking actions, with applications in robotics and cognitive-load measurement.
dl-groep: Works on large-scale distributed and grid computing infrastructure, especially authentication, trust and access control for research e-infrastructures, and cluster workload characterisation. Earlier work was in experimental nuclear physics.
as-harma: Works on audio and speech signal processing, including frequency-warped processing, automatic recognition of bird song, acoustic surveillance and augmented-reality audio. More recent work addresses ambient intelligence and context-aware AI.
e-hortal-quesada: Works on brain–computer interfaces and multimodal affect recognition, decoding movement intention and attention from EEG and EMG signals. Applications include robot-arm control, rehabilitation exoskeletons, and adaptive learning systems for learners with intellectual disabilities.
ai-iamnitchi: Works on large-scale distributed systems: peer-to-peer networks (including early Gnutella mapping), grid and cloud computing, edge computing, and the analysis of complex and social networks. Co-authored the widely cited vision paper on edge-centric computing.
jmh-karel: Develops signal-processing and time-series methods for biomedical data, notably singular spectrum decomposition and measures of neural synchronisation. These are applied mainly to cardiac electrophysiology and ECG analysis, as well as multi-omics studies of atherosclerosis.
a-kasimati: Works on digital and precision agriculture: the economic and environmental benefits of digital farming technologies, decision-support visualisation, UAV remote sensing, and deep learning for diagnosing crop nutrient deficiencies.
sm-kelk: Works on algorithms for phylogenetics: building and comparing phylogenetic networks, computational complexity of reconstruction problems, and graph-theoretic methods. These are applied to evolutionary biology and genomics.
c-kouzinopoulos: Works on the Internet of Things and embedded and high-performance computing. His OpenAlex record is dominated by large CERN collaboration papers from earlier computing work at the LHC, so the topics shown overstate particle physics; he is placed under Computing Paradigms by his departmental research line.
b-kuppers: Works on secure digital assessment in higher education: bring-your-own-device e-exams, threat models for cheating, and tools that detect it. Also has an applied line on near-infrared sorting of textile waste for recycling.
ww-loh: A methodologist working on causal inference and statistical modelling, particularly mediation analysis, confounding adjustment and structural equation modelling. The methods are applied mainly in psychology and behavioural health research.
sj-maubach: A pure mathematician working in affine algebraic geometry and commutative algebra, including locally nilpotent derivations, polynomial automorphisms and cancellation problems. Also has earlier work on information-theoretic analysis of physical unclonable functions.
bjm-mennink: A cryptographer working on symmetric-key primitives and authenticated encryption, including the Chaskey MAC and ISAP, with provable-security analyses of tweakable block ciphers and of releasing unverified plaintext.
d-mestel: Works on formal and quantitative security, including information-flow quantification in interactive systems and formal analysis of replay attacks against vote privacy. Also has work in combinatorics on sequence deletions.
m-mihalak: Works on algorithms and combinatorial optimisation: approximation algorithms for dominating sets in unit disk graphs, network discovery and verification, and optimisation of freight-train formation and railway shunting.
r-mockel: Works on robotics, especially modular and reconfigurable robots such as Roombots and YaMoR, locomotion control with central pattern generators, and bio-inspired legged robots.
m-musegaas: Works in cooperative game theory and operations research: sequencing games, core allocations for vaccination problems, cooperation among streaming platforms, and Stackelberg games for defending crop production.
r-nanda: Works on natural language processing for legal and labour-market text: identifying national implementations of EU directives, detecting bias and fraud in job advertisements, and extracting skills. Also studies traceability of cryptocurrency in darknet markets.
rlm-peeters: Works on systems theory, control and system identification, and on signal-processing methods for cardiac electrophysiology, including electrocardiographic imaging and computational analysis of repolarisation variability.
m-pietrasik: Works on knowledge graphs and machine learning, including inducing class taxonomies from knowledge graphs and graph neural networks. Applied work targets industrial digitalisation, such as the chemical process industry and plastics recycling.
mc-popa: Works on computer vision for human behaviour: action recognition, multimodal audio-visual emotion recognition, and analysing behaviour from surveillance and depth sensors. Applications include retail analytics and care for Parkinson's and Alzheimer's patients.
td-rienstra: Works on formal argumentation and logic in AI: strategic argumentation with opponent models, dynamics of abstract argumentation, and probabilistic argumentation. Has also worked on SHACL shape reasoning with description logics.
l-rieswijk: Works in bioinformatics and toxicogenomics: key characteristics of carcinogens and endocrine disruptors, epigenomic effects of toxicants, and the WikiPathways database. Also contributes to FAIR research data practices.
a-sai: Works on blockchain systems, including centralisation in public blockchains, wealth inequality in cryptocurrencies, and the security of cryptocurrency apps. Also assesses whether blockchains suit uses such as healthcare data sharing, and studies their energy footprint.
b-sakcak: Works on robot motion planning, especially sampling-based kinodynamic planning with motion primitives and RRT variants. Also studies human–robot interaction for telepresence robots and mathematical models of cognition.
m-salvioli: Only a partial OpenAlex record could be matched, covering recent work on educational card games for teaching linear algebra. She is placed under Mathematical & Decision Sciences by her departmental research line, which includes evolutionary game theory.
t-schnitzler: Works on usable privacy and security: how people perceive message deletion, managing the privacy of shared online data over time, and threat vectors in Tor circuit establishment. His OpenAlex record also contains publications by an unrelated author with the same name.
gm-schoenmakers: A game theorist working on stochastic and perfect-information games, particularly the existence of subgame-perfect equilibria and the structure of recursive and infinite-horizon games.
jc-scholtes: Works on natural language processing and information retrieval, from early neural approaches to language to text mining in specialised domains such as drug labels and food substitution with graph neural networks.
yc-semerci: Works on language and speech technology and on behaviour modelling for health, including deep-learning models of student flow in e-learning, emotion recognition from physiological signals, and integrated care platforms for people with Parkinson's and Alzheimer's.
d-slenter: Works in bioinformatics and biological knowledge management, as a core developer of the WikiPathways database and of Wikidata as a life-sciences knowledge graph. Also contributed to the COVID-19 Disease Map.
en-smirnov: Works on machine learning methods, including version spaces, reliable classification and fraud detection. Collaborates on biomedical applications such as multi-omics analysis of atherosclerosis and mass spectrometry imaging.
djnj-soemers: Works on AI for games, in particular Monte Carlo tree search and general game playing, and contributes to the Ludii general game system. Recent work uses evolution and language models to generate new games.
mfm-sondag: Works on information visualisation and computational geometry: stable treemaps, grid maps and the comparison of time-dependent visualisations. Also studies social epistemic networks.
g-spanakis: Works on natural language processing and legal AI: retrieval-augmented language models for legal question answering, statutory article retrieval, and empirical analysis of the EU Digital Services Act transparency database. Also works on speech translation and social-media text mining.
g-stamoulis: Works on quantum computing and theoretical computer science: quantum architecture search, machine-learning estimation of non-stabiliserness ("magic"), and integrality-gap bounds for semidefinite relaxations.
c-sun: Works on privacy-preserving data science for health: synthetic health data with generative models and differential privacy, and privacy-preserving analytics on vertically partitioned data with the Personal Health Train.
g-tang: Works on neuromorphic computing: spiking neural networks on neuromorphic hardware for energy-efficient robot navigation, SLAM and continuous control, and the NeuroBench benchmarking framework.
f-thuijsman: A game theorist working on stochastic games and equilibria, evolutionary game theory, and mathematical models in biology, including evolutionary game theory applied to understanding and treating cancer.
n-tintarev: Works on explainable AI and recommender systems, with highly cited work on designing and evaluating explanations for recommendations. Current research addresses human-centred evaluation, information retrieval, and the societal effects of AI.
v-urovi: Works on trustworthy health data sharing: blockchain-based consent and data-sharing platforms, privacy-preserving distributed machine learning for medical imaging, and multi-agent systems. Also has work on AI that supports service employees' emotion regulation.
jpc-verhoosel: Works on semantic technologies and data infrastructure for agri-food: smart farming, agri-food logistics, and ontology-based access control for FAIR data. Earlier work concerned scheduling in distributed real-time systems.
gb-weiss: A multi-agent systems researcher, editor of a standard textbook on multiagent systems, working on multiagent learning, negotiation, trust and agent-oriented software engineering.
am-wilbik: Works on fuzzy logic and linguistic summarisation of time series, and more recently on federated learning, including vertical federated learning and federated clustering.
mhm-winands: Works on AI for games and search, with foundational papers on Monte Carlo tree search, including progressive strategies, parallelisation and solvers, and applications to real-time and multi-player games.
a-wodeyar: Works on computational neuroscience: state-space methods for real-time phase estimation, neural oscillations as biomarkers of stroke injury and recovery, and the interaction of epileptic spikes with sleep spindles.
n-yousefimanesh: Works in game theory and industrial organisation, on the existence and characterisation of equilibria in price–quantity competition games.
k-zarkogianni: Works on AI for health, especially diabetes: glucose prediction, long-term complication risk, and intelligent monitoring platforms for type 1 diabetes.
rs-pettit: Teaching-focused appointment. No publication record could be matched, so no research profile is shown.
k-schneider: Lecturer in the department. No publication record could be matched, so no research profile is shown.
x-zhang: Lecturer in the department. No publication record could be matched, so no research profile is shown.
